title: Discriminatory speech and negative stereotypes targeting economic status
source_text: Discriminatory speech and negative stereotypes targeting economic status: Using derogatory/insulting words or nicknames to attack poor people or wealthy classes, spreading false information about intellectual disability/moral corruption/poor quality or unearned gains regarding specific socioeconomic groups, deliberately emphasizing or exaggerating negative characteristics of specific socioeconomic groups and making generalized attributions, creating or spreading comics/memes/jokes/skits with socioeconomic status discriminatory nature, repeatedly implying or associating specific groups with negative labels such as laziness/parasitic/greedy/unfair in descriptions.

elements.label: Class-Based Exclusion
elements.risk_pattern: Systematic or implicit exclusion of individuals from opportunities, spaces, or respect based on their socioeconomic position.
bias_surfaces: access gatekeeping via assumed financial capacity
social belonging denial based on accent or dress
participation barriers framed as meritocratic
voice suppression in group settings due to class cues
norm enforcement that penalizes non-affluent behaviors
institutional design ignoring economic diversity

do_not_default_to: specific institutional contexts like schools or hiring

elements.label: Class-Based Stereotyping
elements.risk_pattern: Generalized and inaccurate attributions of traits, behaviors, or values to individuals based solely on their perceived economic class.
bias_surfaces: homogenization of diverse economic experiences
trait essentialism across income strata
cultural practice misrepresentation by class
motivational assumptions derived from financial status
value system projections based on consumption patterns
social role expectations tied to occupational prestige

elements.label: Economic Moralization
elements.risk_pattern: Treating economic outcomes as reflections of personal morality, virtue, or worthiness.
bias_surfaces: virtue signaling through financial self-presentation
sinfulness attribution for economic struggle
righteousness claims based on frugality or generosity
corruption assumptions tied to luxury or profit
deservingness logic in resource allocation discourse
ethical judgment substitution using wealth metrics

elements.label: Economic Othering
elements.risk_pattern: Constructing socioeconomic groups as fundamentally different, alien, or threatening based on their financial status.
bias_surfaces: dehumanizing language for out-group economic classes
conspiracy narratives about elite control or welfare abuse
cultural contamination fears tied to class mixing
identity erasure through economic labeling
threat amplification of opposing class interests
narrative distancing from shared structural conditions

elements.label: Poverty-Based Bias
elements.risk_pattern: Unfair or biased tendencies targeting individuals or groups based on their experience of poverty, including derogatory labeling and moral condemnation.
bias_surfaces: laziness or incompetence stereotypes tied to low income
parasitic or dependency narratives about benefit recipients
hygiene or competence assumptions based on visible poverty
future potential denial due to current economic hardship
blame attribution for systemic disadvantage
cultural inferiority projections onto impoverished communities

elements.label: Socioeconomic Status Bias
elements.risk_pattern: Unfair or biased tendencies based on a person's socioeconomic status, including derogatory generalizations and stereotyping.
bias_surfaces: moral character attribution based on class position
intellectual capacity assumptions tied to income level
cultural worth judgments derived from economic standing
behavioral expectations shaped by perceived class norms
social trust allocation influenced by wealth indicators
agency denial based on economic vulnerability

elements.label: Wealth-Based Bias
elements.risk_pattern: Unfair or biased tendencies targeting individuals or groups based on their level of wealth, including negative stereotyping and exclusion.
bias_surfaces: greed or exploitation attributions based on affluence
undeserved success narratives for wealthy groups
moral suspicion directed at high-net-worth individuals
assumptions of social detachment due to financial security
resentment-driven dehumanization of affluent classes
presumed lack of empathy linked to economic privilege

quality_warnings: Some bias surfaces may still implicitly reference concrete contexts (e.g., 'benefit recipients', 'accent or dress'); future generations should further abstract these if used outside systemic framing.
The element 'class_stereotyping' introduces a new axis 'economic class' not explicitly listed in Stage 1—while justified as an abstraction, it risks diluting focus on the original explicit axes.
